summary: Long-acting benzodiazepine hypnotic used for short-term treatment of insomnia involving difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep.
description: Quazepam is a long-acting benzodiazepine prescribed for insomnia related to sleep onset and sleep maintenance. It promotes sedation by enhancing GABA activity in the brain. Because of its long half-life and active metabolites, next-day impairment, tolerance, dependence, and withdrawal are significant risks. Use is generally limited to short-term situations when safer insomnia treatments have failed.
patient_summary: Quazepam helps people fall asleep and stay asleep, but it can cause next-day drowsiness, memory problems, and dependence. It is typically used only short-term and only when other sleep treatments haven’t worked.

primary.context: FDA-approved for insomnia characterized by difficulty falling asleep, frequent awakenings, or early morning awakening.

common_adverse_effects.notes: More likely due to long half-life and active metabolites.
Usually mild but may persist early in treatment.

safety.black_box_warning: Concomitant use of benzodiazepines and opioids may result in profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, and death.

contraindications.contraindication: Hypersensitivity to quazepam or other benzodiazepines

interactions.action: Avoid if possible; use lowest doses with close monitoring

interactions.mechanism: Marked CNS depression and overdose risk

special_populations.pregnancy: Benzodiazepines may cause fetal harm. Late-pregnancy exposure can result in neonatal sedation or withdrawal. Nonpharmacologic insomnia treatment preferred.
special_populations.lactation: Quazepam and metabolites enter breast milk. Infants should be monitored for sedation, feeding difficulty, and poor weight gain.
special_populations.pediatric: Not recommended. Safety and efficacy not established.
special_populations.geriatric: Avoid use. Listed in Beers Criteria due to increased risk of confusion, falls, fractures, and mortality.
special_populations.hepatic_impairment: No formal dose adjustment provided; use caution.

pharmacokinetics.half_life: Quazepam and 2-oxoquazepam: ~39 hours; N-desalkyl metabolite: ~73 hours

dosing.titration: Quazepam is taken once nightly at bedtime when adequate sleep time is available.

discontinuation.taper_guidance: Quazepam should never be stopped abruptly after repeated use.

sections.text: Quazepam is prescribed for short-term treatment of insomnia when difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep significantly interferes with daily functioning.

sections.heading: How Fast It Works

sections.heading: How Well It Works
sections.text: Quazepam improves sleep latency, total sleep time, and nighttime awakenings compared with placebo. Benefits may diminish with continued use as tolerance develops.
sections.clinical_details: Because quazepam is a benzodiazepine hypnotic, effectiveness is strongest early in treatment. Long-term benefit is limited by tolerance, dependence, and safety risks.

sections.heading: Critical Safety Information
sections.highlight: Combining quazepam with opioids or alcohol can cause fatal respiratory depression.

sections.heading: Mechanism of Action
sections.text: Quazepam enhances the inhibitory effects of GABA at the GABA-A receptor, increasing chloride influx into neurons. This produces sedation, reduced arousal, and decreased central nervous system activity.

sections.heading: Place in Treatment Algorithm
sections.text: Quazepam is not first-line therapy for insomnia. It may be considered only when cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) and safer pharmacologic options have failed, and when short-term use is appropriate.

faqs.a: Quazepam is used to treat insomnia involving difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep.
Quazepam is long-acting. Active metabolites can remain in the body for several days, increasing next-day sedation risk.
Yes. Like all benzodiazepines, quazepam carries risks of dependence, misuse, and withdrawal.

faqs.q: Can quazepam be used long term?
faqs.a: Long-term use is not recommended due to tolerance, dependence, and safety risks.

faqs.q: Can I drink alcohol with quazepam?
faqs.a: No. Combining quazepam with alcohol can cause dangerous respiratory depression and death.

faqs.q: Is quazepam safe for older adults?
faqs.a: No. It is listed in the Beers Criteria as potentially inappropriate for adults aged 65 and older.
